citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, every component of which has nonempty boundary. The ambient sphere has its standard orientation. The normal-transfer expression $B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a symmetric integral bilinear pairing on the free finite-rank group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, with rational extension. It restricts on each component to its normal-transfer pairing; for cycles $a,b$ on distinct components its value is $2\operatorname{lk}(a,b)$, which need not vanish.

Suppose an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks, on distinct components. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus and round the seams to obtain $F'$. There is an integral basis in which $B_{F'}$ has matrix $G\oplus[0]$, where $G$ is the entire matrix of $B_F$, including its cross-component entries. Thus its signature is unchanged. The boundary link and its surface collar remain fixed, so $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$, computed from boundary normal push-offs, is unchanged as well.

A finite sequence of such tubes exists making $F$ connected. All intermediate surfaces still have the original boundary link and collar, no closed components, and finite smooth disk-and-band presentations on their components. The signature and $e$ are preserved throughout.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface with no closed components, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, and let $\alpha$ be a smoothly and properly embedded arc in $F$. Cut $F$ along a sufficiently small open rectangular neighborhood of $\alpha$ and round the resulting boundary corners inside $F$, obtaining $F'$. Then every component of $F'$ has nonempty boundary, the inclusion induces an injection $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)\hookrightarrow H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and its full normal-transfer pairing is the pullback of that on $F$. In particular positive or negative definiteness is preserved by this cut.

Writing $c(F)$ for the number of connected components and $b_1(F)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$, one has
$$b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+1-c(F').$$
More precisely, if the arc does not separate its component, then $c(F')=c(F)$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)-1$; if it separates its component, then $c(F')=c(F)+1$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)$. For a finite disjoint family of $m$ proper arcs, successive cuts retain the injection and pairing assertions and give $b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+m-c(F')$.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be an
oriented link with $r\ge1$ components and complement $X_L$,
([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]]), and let
$$\varphi:H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z$$
be the **total linking homomorphism**, defined as the composite
$$H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\mathrm{Alex}}\widetilde H^1(L;\mathbb Z)\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^rH^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\text{sum}}\mathbb Z,$$
where the first arrow is Alexander duality
([[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]]),
each $H^1(K_i;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ is the orientation-induced
identification, and the last map sums the $r$ coordinates. By
[[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]] the map $\varphi$
may again be written $\pi_1(X_L)\to H_1(X_L)\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathbb Z$; we
denote both composites by $\varphi$ and set $K:=\ker\varphi$.

The **one-variable Alexander module** of $L$ is
$$A_L:=H_1(\widetilde{X_L};\mathbb Z),$$
the first singular homology of the connected infinite cyclic cover
$p:\widetilde{X_L}\to X_L$ classified by $K$
([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]],
[[lem-subgroup-quotient-of-universal-cover]],
[[def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods]]), equipped with its
structure of module over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) in which $t$ acts by the deck
transformation corresponding to the positive generator of
$\operatorname{Deck}(\widetilde{X_L}/X_L)\cong\mathbb Z$.

**Caveats.** The cover is the one classified by $K=\ker\varphi$; since $K$ is
normal the cover is regular and its deck group is
$\pi_1(X_L)/K\cong\mathbb Z$
([[def-regular-covering]], [[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]], [[cor-deck-group-of-a-regular-covering]],
[[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]]). The module $A_L$ is ordinary
integral homology of the cover, with the deck action as its module structure;
no twisting by a representation of the link group is used. The total linking
homomorphism satisfies $\varphi(\mu_i)=1$ for a meridian $\mu_i$ of any one
component, so $r\ge1$ is needed for $\varphi$ to be interesting and $A_L$
depends on the orientations of all components through this map.

derivations.claim: Since $R>2r$, the cylindrical radius of $a_m(\theta,t)$ is positive. Its polar angle recovers $\theta$ modulo $2\pi$, and its radial and vertical displacements recover $t$ on that angle's band interval. Its two derivatives are independent: the $\theta$ derivative has a nonzero angular component and the $t$ derivative is a nonzero vector in its radial-vertical plane. The stated endpoint identification matches the map and all derivatives. Thus it is a smooth embedded band, an annulus for even $m$ and a Möbius band for odd $m$. It retracts onto its oriented core $a_m(\theta,0)$, giving $H_1(A_m;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$.

On that core the band normal lies in the radial-vertical plane and rotates by $m\pi$ during one core circuit. The plane's positively oriented frame for the core orientation is radial-outward followed by negative vertical. The band transverse tangent has coordinates $(\cos(m\theta/2),\sin(m\theta/2))$ in this frame. The surface normal is its fixed quarter-turn, so its angular change is also $m\pi$. The reference longitude given by a constant radial-outward push has linking zero: it is a concentric planar circle. If $m$ is even, each of the two normal lifts is one longitude plus $m/2$ positive meridians; if $m$ is odd, the single lifted circle makes two core circuits and has $m$ positive meridians in total. Hence in either case [F4] gives linking $m$ with the core. By [F1] the normal pairing of $A_m$ is therefore the one-by-one matrix $[m]$.

In the boundary sum a small thickening of $F$ together with half its product neck meets a small thickening of $A_m$ with the other half in a rectangle. The overlap is contractible and the neck connects the band to just the chosen component of $F$. The degree-zero overlap map is injective. Thus [F3] gives $H_1(F^*;\mathbb Z)=H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\oplus H_1(A_m;\mathbb Z)$, induced by the two old inclusions; also $c(F^*)=c(F)$. Choose old cycles away from the boundary attaching interval, and use the band core for the last basis class. Their old-old linking entries are unchanged. The band core and its short normal transfers lie in the separated band ball, while the old cycles and transfers lie outside it, so all mixed linking numbers vanish: the core cycles bound chains in their ball, disjoint from those old cycles. The full matrix is therefore $G\oplus[m]$, even if $G$ itself has nonzero cross-component entries. Consequently this full form is positive definite when $G$ is positive definite and $m>0$, and negative definite in the corresponding negative case.

The core of $A_m$ crosses its co-core $\alpha'$ once and misses the boundary-sum neck and the part of $\alpha''$ on $F$. Arrange the small endpoint joining charts away from this crossing. Thus it is a closed curve on the affected component of $F^*$ crossing $\alpha''$ transversely exactly once. A separating proper arc would force every closed curve to cross it an even number of times: crossings alternate between its two complementary components, and a closed curve returns to its starting component. This parity statement does not require orientability. Therefore $\alpha''$ is nonseparating on its component.

Apply [F2] to the cut along $\alpha''$. Its pairing is a restriction through an injective homology map of the definite form in step 3.1, so it has the same strict sign. Every resulting component has nonempty boundary. Since the cut is nonseparating by step 4.1, [F2] gives $c(F_m)=c(F^*)=c(F)$ and $b_1(F_m)=b_1(F^*)-1$. Step 3.1 gives $b_1(F^*)=b_1(F)+1$, proving the asserted first-Betti-number equality. These arguments allow the specified initial disconnected and nonorientable surfaces; neither the product neck nor the cut changes their untreated components.

boundaries.reason: A nonempty boundary link and spanning surfaces without closed components are assumed.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement allows zero first Betti number and zero signature; no inverse of the normal form is taken.
The Statement allows a one-component link and connected or disconnected surfaces satisfy the same argument.
The Statement uses the signature, which is the difference of positive and negative ranks; the proof does not require nonsingularity.
The Statement retains the same literal boundary link, with arbitrary component orientations.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC, which is assumed and inherited through the cited linking and smooth construction suppliers.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from the full normal-transfer pairing, linking number and arc-cut suppliers. The parametrized band, product neck and homology computations are finite.

risk_review.notes: Preserves full disconnected and nonorientable surface scope. All new prerequisite sources and their geometric constructions still require independent owner review.
